messages:
jia: Heads-up — ran into spiky OTLP exporter errors from python inference workers during a burst test. exporter queue filled, process slowed and we saw CPU spin on flush.

sam: Can you paste logs? Is this the OTLP gRPC exporter or the http one?

jia: otlp-grpc, default batch span processor. log snippets: 
```
ERROR exporter: failed to send batch: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = etcd: request timed out
WARNING sdk: exporter queue full, dropping spans
```

eldar: ResourceExhausted often means backend rate-limited. But queue full + GIL in CPython means flush stalls. Did you run with async worker threads?

lex: For rust/go we don't see that pattern — their exporters are async at the runtime level. Python SDK spawns a background thread but flush can block on network.

marta: Two things we should align on: 1) backpressure semantics (drop vs block) 2) how we expose config in the platform (per-tenant queue size + retention sampling).

jia: Proposal: default sampler remains parent-based, but we enable a platform-level tail-sampling hook that can override based on tenant SLO. Also change exporter behavior to "block-but-bounded" for hosted tier, and "drop" for free tier. Thoughts?

sam: Block-but-bounded seems reasonable for Dedicated customers; blocking buys durability but could violate latency SLOs for inference if flush happens on request thread. Need to ensure we never block inference processing threads.

lex: Implementation detail: for python we must avoid calling flush() on request handling path. Use separate flushing daemon and a bounded queue. When queue full: return fast failure metric and optionally drop spans. For rust we can leverage tokio mpsc bounded channel + backpressure via awaiting send — but again don't await on request path.

eldar: We should standardize an SDK shim that provides a non-blocking API for inference processes: e.g., `trace.emit(span)` that never blocks the caller and returns a delivery status via a metric counter. Under the hood it enqueues or signals goroutine/task.

marta: That shim needs to expose config from the console: max_queue_size, max_age_ms, drop_policy (LRU/oldest/new). Also a tenant-level sampling override and retention TTL so we can scrub low-value spans earlier.

jia: Quick config snippet I'm testing: 
```
OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=1000
OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY_MS=100
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://telemetry.redwood.example/v1/traces
OTEL_DROP_POLICY=oldest
```

sam: Another practical: graceful shutdown. Many of these errors surface when a hot restart kills the process before flush. We need SDK hooks and our deploy agent to call `tracer.force_flush(timeout=2s)` and wait. Also communicate in console rollout UX: "rolling restart will signal telemetry flush; expected tail latency increase".

lex: For go/rust we can set the signal handler to attempt flush on SIGTERM and increase Pod terminationGracePeriod for k8s. For python, gunicorn hooks or uvicorn lifespan events can call tracer.shutdown().

eldar: Retention + storage costs — we should add a sampling tier that keeps full spans for error traces and half-rate for normal traffic. Platform can supply sampling rules -> agents fetch rules at startup and update sampler dynamically.

marta: UX question: in the Console, do we show per-tenant dropped-span rates and queue saturation graph? I think yes, it's crucial for debugging.

jia: Agreed. Also alerting: trigger when drop_rate > 1% for 5m or when exporter retry error rate spikes.

sam: One more: exporter retries. We should use exponential backoff with capped jitter client-side. But don't retry forever — after N tries mark spans as failed and increment the drop metric.

deploy-bot: deploy started: telemetry-exporter-shim v0.9.1 -> canary in infra-test cluster (pods=3).

jia: I'll run the burst test against canary and post results. If we can get a reproducible path and add metrics for queue_size/drops/flush_latency we can finalize the default config.

marta: Plan: jia validates, lex writes shim for go/rust parity, edlar wires sampler update API, sam updates k8s termination hooks, I'll design console graphs and alerts. Back to you all.
